New Community Creative Activation Fund for Creative Places Baltinglass 
Wicklow County Council has announced an extension of the Creative Places Baltinglass Programme, 
along with the introduction of a new Community Creative Activation Fund for Baltinglass.  
The initial three-year programme began in 2022 and concluded in June 2025, during which the Arts 
Council invested a total of €375,000. In the second two-year phase, the Arts Council has awarded 
Wicklow County Council's Arts Office €170,000 of a maximum €180,000 which was available in this new 
extension of the application process.  
The Fund is designed to facilitate continued engagement between communities and artists and projects 
must involve paid creative personnel. Applications could include proposals for residencies, event series, 
creative public realm projects and a variety of other initiatives. Grants will range from €3,000 to €5,000 for 
any single application.  
OFFICIAL OPENING OF BRAY TRANSPORT INTERCHANGE 
Minister of State with responsibility for International and Road Transport, Logistics, Rail and Ports, Séan 
Canney officially opened the Bray Transport Interchange on 17th September, on behalf of Wicklow County 
Council in partnership with the National Transport Authority (NTA).  
This project has successfully delivered a high-quality transport interchange that facilitates seamless 
connections between key modes of transportation including walking, cycling, taxis, buses and railway 
services. The completed scheme has created a safer, more connected and high-quality public realm 
environment that complements the heritage of the station building while promoting development in the 
area.  
Wicklow County Council’s Active Travel Vision aims for every resident in County Wicklow to use active 
travel options in their daily lives naturally and without hesitation. The Council has provided practical and 
safe options for residents to do so.  
At the Bray Transport Interchange, Wicklow County Council, with funding and support from the 
Department of Transport through the NTA, has created a high-quality environment and a focal point for 
commuters and visitors. The improved and safer facilities around Bray Train Station will encourage more 
people to adopt sustainable methods of transport in their everyday lives.

Capital Assistance Scheme (CAS) 
Under CAS, the Department is accepting applications for capital funding for the delivery, through either

elderly. 
•

•

settings into community-based living. 
 
Assessment criteria 
CAS funding operates in partnership with Local Authorities and Approved Housing Bodies.

homelessness.  
➢ Liaising with specific households to establish their specific needs.  
➢ Establishing relationships with local property agents and landlords; and,  
➢ Supporting those homeless households to (a) prevent the necessity to enter emergency 
accommodation or (b) to exit emergency accommodation and secure a tenancy.

➢ To date, 656 households (457 families & 198 singles) have been assisted under the Homeless HAP

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in 
danger of becoming homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation.

Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed 
units, and two 3-bed units. Eleven families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning to 
a permanent home and the resulting vacancies are in the process of being occupied with families 
experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully 
operational. Wicklow County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they 
continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
 
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved 
Housing Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular 
support needs of the clients. Six of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully 
moved into their forever homes and this in turn created space to move further people out of 
homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful. 
 
Housing First 
Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-East 
Region. Wicklow County Council is committed to working with them and has now reached and surpassed 
the targets identified in the programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home provides the basis

1.1.1 
Blessington Town Centre First Masterplan  
Blessington, as a Pathfinder Town, is leading the way in the development of a Town Centre First 
Masterplan. This masterplan offers a clear and strategic framework for the positive and sustainable 
development of the town, both in the short term and in the future. Currently, the implementation of the Town 
Centre First (TCF) plan is in the planning stage, focusing on revitalising key areas in the town. 
 
Rural Regeneration and Development Fund (RRDF) funding has been allocated specifically to redesign 
Main Street and Market Square, two central areas that will play a significant role in the town's regeneration. 
The goal is to bring these projects to a shovel-ready stage, which means they will be fully prepared for the 
next phase, where they can be submitted for Category 1 RRDF funding to secure further financial support 
for construction and development. This initiative is a significant step toward enhancing the town's 
infrastructure, economic vitality, and overall community appeal.

Newtownmountkennedy was one of 26 towns selected nationally under Phase 2 of the Town Centre First 
Plan initiative. The town received €30,000 in funding to support the development of its own Town Centre 
First Plan, aimed at guiding the revitalisation and sustainable development of the town centre, transforming 
it into a vibrant and thriving hub for the community. The funding was provided under the Town Centre First 
Measure 2 Suite of Supports. The plan was originally required to be completed, and all associated claims 
submitted to the Department by 5th September 2025; however, an extension to 14th November 2025 was 
granted.

Regeneration Officer (TRO), in collaboration with the Town Team, drafted and issued a tender document 
for the development of the Town Centre First (TCF) Plan. The contract was awarded to ACT (Accelerating 
Change Together), and the process of compiling the TCF Plan is currently underway. Of the three planned 
public consultation workshops, the first took place in June 2025, the second is scheduled for August 2025, 
and the third and final workshop will be held in September 2025.

Spongeworks EU horizon programme: 
Wicklow County Council in partnership with the Wicklow Uplands Council, the East Wicklow Rivers Trust and LAWPRO 
have been selected to participate in an EU horizon programme called SpongeWorks. Each participating region will work 
on strategy to develop and scale sponge measures – Nature based Solutions that help retain water, reduce flood or 
drought risk and restore ecosystems.  
Wicklow’s project explores restoring the upper Aughrim River’s capacity to slow water flow. SpongeWorks is a leading 
Horizon Europe initiative in nature-based climate adaption, bringing together 28 partners and 23 knowledge institutions. 
The project is developing practical, scalable solutions for sponge measures implementation which address critical 
questions about effectiveness, financing, governance and stakeholder engagement.  
The EU Horizon Spongeworks project has now commenced. The first task is to complete an implementation plan with 
actions and deliverables which must be approved by the programme. Wicklow County Council can now draw down the 
first 25% of the projects €93,300 budget.

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant  
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Market Surveillance & Construction Product Regulations which is one of the key roles of Building Control.

Information Systems 
 
Operations  
 
• 
The IT Helpdesk continues to streamline the workflow for the technical support team with an average of 50 tickets 
a day this month, providing assistance for both in-house and remote workers.  
 
GIS & Systems Analysis 
• 
Fire Hydrant Mapping for Fire Service 
We supported the Fire Service in locating fire hydrants using our GIS mapping tools. This ensures 
firefighters can quickly identify hydrant locations during emergencies, improving public safety. 
 
• 
Food Poverty & Food Environment Mapping 
Updates were made to the Wicklow Food Poverty and Food Environment mapping applications. New data 
was processed and added in partnership with Bray and North Wicklow Area Partnership. These tools help 
community groups and local authorities understand access to food resources across the county. 
 
• 
Residential & Population Analysis (Forward Planning) 
Significant progress was made on our interactive planning tools. A new GIS viewer was updated to include 
zoning, CSO, housing, and transport data. We also created a new layer to track planning permissions that 
are under construction but not yet completed, supporting better monitoring of development across Wicklow. 
 
• 
Roads Data & Mapping 
The Roads Schedule for 2025 was obtained and integrated into all existing GIS applications. This provides 
an up-to-date record of the county’s road network for planning and operational purposes. 
 
• 
Landownership Records 
New landownership data was procured from the Property Registration Authority of Ireland (PRAI). This 
information will support planning, corporate services, and climate action projects. 
 
• 
Map Production for Roads Department 
A series of new maps were created for the Roads Department, including updated schedules and supporting 
documents. These maps are used to guide maintenance and infrastructure planning. 
 
Infrastructure 
• 
Ongoing upgrades of WAN connections at remote sites by Wicklow County Council aim to optimize performance 
and cost-effectiveness.
